Convert between plot coordinates and a standard space

Source: R/mni.R
mesh_to_mni.Rd

mesh_to_mni() takes coordinates as the plot draws them and returns where they are in a standard space; mni_to_mesh() goes the other way, which is what you want for putting add_points() somewhere specific.

Usage

mesh_to_mni(
  x,
  y,
  z,
  hemisphere = c("lh", "rh"),
  surface = "pial",
  space = c("mni305", "mni152")
)

mni_to_mesh(
  x,
  y,
  z,
  hemisphere = c("lh", "rh"),
  surface = "pial",
  space = c("mni305", "mni152")
)

Arguments

x, y, z

Numeric coordinates.

hemisphere

"lh" or "rh" – which hemisphere's shift applies.

surface

The surface the coordinates belong to. One of "white", "pial", "midthickness", "smoothwm" or "orig".

space

"mni305", which fsaverage is, or "mni152".

Value

A data.frame of x, y and z.

Details

The surfaces are fsaverage5, and fsaverage is an MNI305 average, so their coordinates already are MNI305 apart from a shift: each hemisphere is moved so it meets the midline at x = 0, which is what lets the two be drawn together. These functions add or remove that shift, reading it from the mesh rather than assuming it, so a rebuilt mesh cannot silently put every point in the wrong place.

space = "mni152" applies FreeSurfer's published MNI305-to-MNI152 transform on top. Across the brain that moves a coordinate by two to three millimetres.

Only anatomical surfaces can be converted. An inflated or spherical surface has had every vertex moved, so a position on it does not correspond to a place in the brain, and asking is an error rather than a number that looks usable.

Examples

# where does a point in MNI space sit in the plot?
mni_to_mesh(-42, -20, 55, hemisphere = "lh")
#>           x   y  z
#> 1 -43.22156 -20 55

# and back again
mesh_to_mni(-43.2, -20, 55, hemisphere = "lh")
#>           x   y  z
#> 1 -41.97844 -20 55
